reviews.review: Bought this to relive the glory days of MP and had fun my first few matches, until i crashed two time in my last two matches right before extraction. Only got it due to it being discounted, game sometimes starts with no audio and while a restart fixes it is pretty annoying. Thank god the servers are still up but man wish they showed some love to this surviving community of COOP players.

I used the play the multiplayer of this a lot on the xbox back in the day. The legendary edition didn't have the multiplayer but surprisingly this still has it and the servers are curently up. I even found a mod that allows native controller support which is a bit odd that it wasn't there in the first place but whatever.

The mechanics in ME3 are so smooth and functional.  The story is amazing in however what decisions you make to impact to the final mission.  On another note, I think I can understand how some of the other players were baffled on the core ending, but I won't spoil anything.  The multiplayer is great, and even better when you have a cohesive and communicating team.

I have played Mass Effect 3 Coop (Galaxy at War Online) for thousands of hours on 360 and PS3 and it is some of the best coop there is. There are so many characters and often more than 1 viable build for each one. I recently started playing on PC and the poor framerates and glitches on 360/PS3 seem to be mostly not present. It takes quite a while to unlock all the characters and Gear Bonuses. Even longer to unlock all the weapons but that is part of the fun. The newer Legendary Edition did not include the Coop which is incredibly unfortunate so get the individual Mass Aeffect 3 game to get the Coop. Join the N7 today!

The Multiplayer which dookies all over other Horde shooters like Gears of Bore is still active, and I was able to import my ME3 LE Shepard into OG3 just by dragging and dropping the save. Absolutely worth your time for the multi alone.

If BioWare wanted to curry some goodwill with disenfranchised fans, they should add a launcher to Legendary Edition that opens the Multiplayer. There's a large community of die-hards still playing and I find games in it faster than I do in garbage like Halo: Infinite. 

I wish they would remove the EA App launcher though, I went through two days of headache getting it to stop ctd'ing on Windows 11 and thankfully a multiplayer regular reached out and told me his solution.

The Mass Effect Trilogy never grows old. This version has lost the ability to take an imported Shepard from Mass Effect 2 but you can still use the interactive comic when starting a new character to change the default starting conditions. With mass Effect 2 it takes up less than half the space on your disk than the Mass Effect Legendary Edition.

Works fine out of the box on linux (POP!_OS).
Some stutters here and there but after switching to proton it's now gone.
Sadly controllers don't work with this game - steamdeck doesn't work even with other controller layouts.

Game itself is fun to play, for my liking the comic part when you create a new game could be shortened.
Some stuff is unclear had a while until I figured out how to open a door.

I'm just going to get this out of the way first: everything people said was bad about the ending? none of them were wrong. it's an ABC choose your ending setup and none of the presented options make sense. but what people neglected to mention back when this was a raging controversy is just how much the rest of the game NAILS everything about the story that led up to it. 

tuchanka, rannoch, cerberus, even miranda's personal story, multiple plot threads that had been building over multiple games were drawn to a close in a way that respected your choices across the trilogy. depending on whether or not you killed wrex all the way back in *the first game* you may very well end up with a different outcome from what you wanted. it's a testament to the writing and development teams just how everything before that crapsack ending was so close to perfection. 

the gameplay as well is the best the franchise has ever had. it finally nailed the mix of rpg to shooter, taking the lessons learned from 2 and combining them with the better mechanics of 1. the amount of weapons at your disposal is insane, along with weapon mods, and the game now uses a shield health hybrid similar to halo that gives medi-gel more of a purpose than simply reviving squad members (although it still does that) while making it less of a crutch than it was in 1. 

one other flaw I've just remembered is that it does a worse job with side quest management. it's far too easy to miss certain quests and not be able to complete them, it's also possible to get a quest from someone 5-6 hours before you can actually do it. and when you do miss a quest, it isn't removed from your journal, so I spent most of the game wondering if I had missed certain quests when it actually turned out they were uncompletable before nearly the end of the game. 

while the beginning was a bit rough and the very end was worthy of the controversy it caused, the middle is the closest thing to a perfect mass effect game anyone has ever made. I'm usually someone who thinks a bad ending can ruin the rest of the experience- but not this time. the rest is just too good to be brought down. godlike game.
i love mass effect and garrus vakarian.
I played. I took control. I cried.
Great run on from the previous games.  Need to play previous games first to get the complete story.  Newer players hooked on quick successes and FPS games will find it tiresome.
